findings.summary: total() is checked only for being truthy, so a wrong or subtracted booking fee passes.
findings.reason: test_total_for_a_family runs total() and prints the result, but asserts only `assert result`. Subtracting the fee (1350) or charging 151 cents (1651) is still truthy, so all three mutants survive.

suggestion.assertion_or_input: assert result == 1650 (1000 adult + 500 senior + 150 booking fee), instead of assert result

findings.criticality_reason: money: the amount charged for a booking

findings.summary: The concession boundary at 65 is untested: no test uses age 64 or 65.
findings.reason: The tests price ages 30 and 70 only. Moving the boundary (age > 65, or CONCESSION_AGE = 66) changes nothing for either age, so a 65-year-old could lose the discount without a test failing.

suggestion.assertion_or_input: ages 64 (full fare) and 65 (half fare), the boundary the docstring promises

findings.criticality_reason: money: who gets the half-fare concession

findings.summary: The goodwill credit can change without a test noticing, because no test cancels by the operator.
findings.reason: GOODWILL_CENTS is a module constant: the line runs when the module is imported, so every refund test covers it, but it is only used in the operator-cancellation branch, which no test reaches (G1).
findings.criticality_reason: money: what an operator cancellation refunds

findings.summary: while i < len(passengers) and while i != len(passengers) behave the same here.
findings.reason: i starts at 0 and only i += 1 changes it, and nothing in the loop changes passengers, so i counts up through 0, 1, ... and meets len(passengers) exactly (a length is never negative). Both conditions first become false at that same step, for every list.

findings.summary: Eight mutants of the INFO log line in total() survive; the log text is not behaviour anyone relies on.
findings.reason: They change only the log call: its text, its arguments, or whether it is made. Nothing parses the message. With INFO logging on, M19 and M20 make logging print a formatting error to stderr, but the call never raises, so the price is unaffected.

coverage_gaps.note: No test calls refund_cents with cancelled_by_operator=True, so the new operator-cancellation branch (lines 15-17) never runs. mutmut reported its 8 mutants there as survived because it tracks tests per function; per-test line coverage shows no test executed these lines, so they are no_coverage here.
coverage_gaps.suggestion: Add a test that cancels by the operator (tests/test_refunds.py): refund_cents(999, 1, cancelled_by_operator=True) == 1499. The same test closes F3.

summary.headline: In the 3 changed files, total() is never checked for the right amount (P0), the 65+ concession boundary is untested (P1), the goodwill credit can change unnoticed (P2), and no test reaches the new operator-cancellation refund. The builtin engine killed 18 of 29 mutants (62.1%) and mutmut 17 of 33 (51.5%); the two use different operators, so the scores are not comparable.

by_engine.score_text: builtin: 18 of 29 mutants killed in 3 changed files (62.1%); 1 equivalent excluded, 1 timed out (19 of 30, 63.3%, counting timeouts and runtime errors as kills)
mutmut: 17 of 33 mutants killed in 3 changed files (51.5%); 1 timed out (18 of 34, 52.9%, counting timeouts and runtime errors as kills)

limitations: Scope is the changed lines in examples/fare-calc/change.diff. The refund tiers that already existed were not mutated (mutmut made 7 mutants there; they were dropped as out of scope).
The two engines use different operators: mutmut leaves module constants alone and the builtin engine adds i < n -> i != n. Their scores are reported separately and are not comparable or additive.
A mutation score says these mutants were killed; it says nothing about faults these operators cannot express.
mutmut ran under WSL (Python 3.12) because mutmut 3 needs fork(); the baseline, the builtin engine and the proofs ran on Windows (Python 3.14). Both read the same files.
One mutant per engine looped forever (i += 0, i = 1) and was stopped by the timeout; timeouts are not counted as kills in the main score.
The suggested tests were proved in scratch copies and not written to the repository (write_tests: false).
